classification: manual-hardware-test candidate; no GPU executed during build, packaging or review

change_since_previous_delivery.kernel: vmmap registration failure now returns -ENOMEM and each caller rolls back with the primitive that matches its registry (pmap_unmapdev for the device path, nmx_xnu_unmap for vmap); plus the new ring space/wrap fixture, which changes no runtime behaviour

reuse_basis: the pins in sources.json and acceleration/sources.json are unchanged since 991e460
the nmx_drm_uapi.h hunks in xkpi.patch are byte identical to the ones at 991e460
acceleration/sources.json, acceleration/patches/**, probe/**, build_userland.sh and stage.py are unchanged since 991e460
the probe includes only the C/C++ standard library and vulkan.h, no kernel header
the drm-kmod.patch additions since then touch i915 GT/tasklet/pcode only and the freebsd.patch additions touch linuxkpi locks only; neither touches a UAPI header

metal.note: unchanged signed bundle carried over from the previous delivery; outside this stage's scope

verification_performed_here: every component zip digest was compared with its GitHub API digest and the values were asserted by the packaging script
the assembler refused unless the kernel artifact carried 1250 unit logs, exact all/i915/runtime source counts, every required fixture marker and a passed KC preflight
the packaged SHA256SUMS was re-verified file by file: 0 mismatches
the kext binary in the package is byte identical to the CI artifact binary
the probe binary in the package is byte identical to the 991e460 artifact binary
the booting EFI config digest still matches 22a185d96105258fc24b0d0ca842206dc36fc885fbb8b7d0559e58bf1ae2f6f9, so no boot configuration was changed
the copy on the USB was hashed after writing and matches the packaged digest; the boot EFI config digest was re-checked after delivery and is unchanged, so the boot configuration was not touched
the previous USB pointer files were copied into the delivery folder before being replaced, so the earlier instructions are still recoverable
how_to_confirm_the_loaded_version: the packaged run-probe.sh does it: it compares the loaded kext's LC_UUID from kextstat against the staged binary's LC_UUID and records both, failing on any mismatch
manually, if ever needed: shasum -a 256 on the installed NMXGPU and probe/uhd770-compute-probe, compared with the two binary_sha256 values above
the probe prints its stage log to the session directory, which the report carries back
does_not_prove: any GPU execution, completion, cache visibility, physical interrupt or machine stability
that the reused 991e460 userland actually works with this kernel; the reuse is an interface argument, not a run
Metal, WindowServer or display acceleration, which are later stages

acceptance_for_this_package.success: in one macOS session on the target: 8086:4680 with the recorded binaries, GPU executes the varying workloads, every output word compares, COMPUTE_READBACK_VERIFIED is printed before teardown, the process exits 0 and the system shows no panic, hang or GPU timeout
acceptance_for_this_package.failure: collect the session report folder; the last recorded stage names the failing edge, and another package is prepared only after that edge is traced in source

recovery_entry_check.finding: the machine currently boots with -nvoff, so the driver is disabled by the live boot configuration; the package's config.safe.plist is byte identical to that live config, config.test.plist drops -nvoff to enable the driver, and reference-efi/config.optout-reference.plist keeps a no-GPU reference for recovery. The delivery itself modified no boot file.
recovery_entry_check.limits: this verifies the files, not that OpenCore selects them on the next boot; only the target boot can show which configuration was actually applied

test_harness_verification.method: static review of the packaged scripts and of the safe/test boot configurations; nothing was executed

boot_flag_contract.test_config: -v debug=0x100 keepsyms=1 -igfxvesa alcid=11 amfi=0x80 ipc_control_port_options=0 nmxintel=1 nmxdiagdelay=180
boot_flag_contract.finding: the prepare step installs the test config, whose only change against the live safe config is that -nvoff becomes nmxintel=1 plus the diagnostic delay

refusals_before_any_gpu_work: Run-UHD770-Test.command refuses without root, without /bin/bash -p, on a non-Darwin host, or before PREPARED (missing installed coordinator)
session.sh test refuses when the current boot is not the preparation boot that was armed
session.sh test refuses on an opt-out boot by matching -nvoff in kern.bootargs, and records next_boot_optout=verified only after restore_optout succeeds
session-user.sh manual refuses without nmxintel=1, without an armed state, without a root-owned per-boot authorization naming this uid, and when the recovery marker says NOT_VERIFIED
session-user.sh manual refuses a second manual session in the same boot, so an incomplete run cannot be repeated by accident

pre_compute_gates.recovery: restore_optout writes the safe config to config.plist.uhd770-pending, re-hashes it, atomically renames it into place, re-hashes and syncs; a config changed independently is preserved and the step fails
pre_compute_gates.recorder: Root restarts the persistent capture job and waits for it to confirm startup before the compute phase
pre_compute_gates.driver: session-user.sh waits up to 330 seconds for next_boot_optout=verified and for IORegistry to show NMXGPU in a ready state, with distinct exits for deadline (124), unverified recovery (65), failed initialization (66), registry failure (67) and gate timeout (68)

log_capture: Start-UHD770.command captures from its first command, including failures before the plan exists, and records the exact ancestor permissions that broke earlier attempts without changing them
it copies the preparation log to a USB volume only when exactly one mounted volume carries this package's exact safe or test EFI bytes; otherwise it keeps the system-disk report and says so
session-user.sh takes a per-boot directory as an atomic lock and writes coordinator_exit into the session record
limits: this is a reading of the scripts, not a run; only the target boot shows which configuration OpenCore applied
if the machine panicked before the boot-time restore, the USB could still hold the test config; reference-efi/config.optout-reference.plist and Restore-UHD770.ps1 are the Windows-side recovery

probe_math_check.method: compared the compute shader in the packaged probe with the CPU expectation in the same probe source
probe_math_check.shader: value = input[i] ^ seed; shift = (i % 31) + 1; rotated = (value << shift) | (value >> (32 - shift)); out[i] = (rotated + i * 0x9e3779b9) ^ (input[i] >> 7)
probe_math_check.cpu: same expression, with input[i] produced by seed ^ (i * 747796405 + 2891336453)
probe_math_check.finding: the GPU and CPU formulas are identical term by term, including that the final xor uses the unrotated input, and the shift stays in 1..31 so no undefined shift can occur; the dispatch covers ceil(count/64) groups of 64 invocations and the probe bounds-checks i against count
probe_math_check.synchronization: host->compute and compute->host pipeline barriers bracket the dispatch, and the readback invalidates non-coherent memory before comparing
probe_math_check.limits: this shows the probe would detect a wrong result rather than agreeing with itself; it does not show the GPU ran

kext_loading_check.method: parsed the packaged kext Info.plist and Mach-O header, and read what the CI preflight actually runs

personality.NMXGPUIntel: IOProviderClass IOPCIDevice, IOPCIPrimaryMatch 0x00008086 & 0x0000ffff (any Intel vendor), IOPCIClassMatch 0x03000000 & 0xff000000 (display class), IOProbeScore 60000
personality.finding: the personality matches 8086:4680 as an Intel display-class PCI device, so attachment does not depend on a hard-coded device ID

binary.amfi_relaxed_by_boot_arg: amfi=0x80 is present in both the safe and the test boot configurations
binary.segments: __TEXT 0xac2000 vmsize, __DATA 0x113000, __LINKEDIT 0x187000; LC_SYMTAB, LC_DYSYMTAB and LC_UUID present

preflight_strength.what_it_does: the CI preflight copies the candidate into a temporary repository, runs kmutil create against the runner's real BootKernelExtensions.kc with --allow-missing-kdk, requires the create to succeed, then kmutil inspect verifies com.nullmoth.NMXGPU is in the produced collection
limits: the runner is macOS 15.5 while the target is 15.7.9; KPI 8.0 libraries are stable but this is not the target build
the temporary collection is deliberately never installed, so the real collection for the test boot is built at prepare time on the target

loaded_version_check_as_implemented.method: read run-probe.sh; the check is part of the packaged test path, not something the user must do by hand
kext_identity: before any probe, run-probe.sh requires the staged NMXGPU Mach-O and extracts its x86_64 LC_UUID
it then reads kextstat -l -b com.nullmoth.NMXGPU, requires exactly one table row with a valid UUID, and fails unless that UUID equals the staged binary's UUID
the bundle name and UUID are appended to loaded-UUIDs.txt and the binary sha256 to payload-SHA256SUMS, so the report carries what was actually loaded
userland_identity: the staged runtime directory is walked and every file is hashed into payload-SHA256SUMS

the ICD is rewritten per session with an absolute library_path to the staged libvulkan_intel.dylib, so the loader never searches globally and the relative-path hazard in the shipped intel_icd.json is avoided
the probe is invoked with --device-id 0x4680, so a different device is rejected rather than tested

vulkan_payload_check.icd_shipped: intel_icd.json with library_path ./libvulkan_intel.dylib (relative to its own directory)
vulkan_payload_check.icd_used: rewritten to an absolute path at the staged runtime directory

dylib_install_names.libvulkan_intel.dylib: @loader_path/libvulkan_intel.dylib, loading @loader_path/libdrm.2.dylib plus libSystem, libz and libc++

vulkan_payload_check.finding: no runner path survives in any install name, so the bundle is self-contained; the shader verify.comp.spv (2060 bytes) ships beside the probe
vulkan_payload_check.probe_arguments: --device-id 0x4680 --count 4099 --iterations 3 --deadline 45, with an outer runner deadline of 55 seconds

limits: this is a reading of the scripts and binaries, not a run
the UUID comparison proves the staged binary is what loaded; it does not prove that binary computes correctly
